subject: Certificate safeguard & DNS health-probe playbook
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ops@atlas-cloud.com
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Certificate safeguard & DNS health-probe playbook

Hi team,

Following our on-call incident last week where a partial certificate chain propagation delay caused a small set of private endpoints to fail during renewal, I sketched a short operator playbook that pairs DNS health probes with cert-swap safeguards. The goal: detect TLS chain/OCSP regressions before the client-visible SLO is impacted and provide an automated safe-rollover path for private VPC endpoints.

High-level proposal:
- Lightweight DNS health probes (internal TTL-aware) that validate: A/AAAA, CNAME split-horizon mappings, and TLS handshakes (complete chain + OCSP stapling).
- Staged cert-swap: first switch a canary routing group (10% of traffic) to the new cert + stapling checks; then widen if probes are clean.
- Emergency rollback: immediately revert SNI mapping and enable the old cert via pre-loaded key material when a probe fails post-cutover.
- Operator checklist: preflight (chain verification, CRL/OCSP endpoint reachability), cutover window, verification window, and rollback steps.

I've attached a runbook draft and a probe checklist (spreadsheet) plus a stub of the probe scripts used in testing. Please review for gaps from the SRE/security side and for any integration constraints with Atlas Cloud's private DNS offerings (ops@atlas-cloud.com cc'd).

Specific asks:
1) Karthik — confirm any VPC gateway constraints for serving an alternate cert on the same FQDN during canary.
2) Laura — review the operator rollback commands and RBAC notes in section 3 of the runbook.
3) Marissa/Atlas — can Atlas provide a short test window (non-prod) to exercise split-horizon propagation under our probe pattern?

Thanks,

Markus
Lead Infra PM
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ops@atlas-cloud.com

Subject: Re: Certificate safeguard & DNS health-probe playbook

Thanks Markus — great initiative. A few quick notes from infra runtime constraints: 

- VPC gateway behavior: on Atlas-managed gateways we can bind multiple certs to the same virtual host but the gateway chooses the cert via SNI. For a canary of the same FQDN we have two realistic options: 1) routing-level split (route a subset of TLS-terminated connections to a canary backend that presents the new cert), or 2) use a short-lived alternate FQDN (canary.<service>.private) that resolves to the canary backends and is mapped in clients via a feature flag. Option (1) is preferable for client transparency but requires gateway support for per-connection backend selection (Atlas supports it with an L7 policy).
- OCSP and stapling: ensure the runbook includes a prefetch/prime window (48h) for new certs to warm OCSP responses from the CA, and a probe that validates both chain and stapled response freshness.

Operational constraints to add to the runbook:
1) Probe rate-limiting to avoid hitting CA/OCSP throttles.
2) Health-probe telemetry ingestion path (export to Console) so we can tie probe regressions to model-service errors.
3) Graceful acceptance for clients that cache A records beyond TTL (probe should validate client-facing resolution via a sampling agent located in the same VPC subnets).

I added inline comments to the runbook PDF and a short appendix suggestion for an automated canary rollback based on probe error thresholds (see JIRA-OPS-1247).

- Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer

Subject: Re: Certificate safeguard & DNS health-probe playbook

Quick review notes — thanks Markus. A few corrections and an ask: 

- RBAC: section 3 lists the runbook operators as a single oncall role. Please split to: cert-ops (can perform CSR/CSR signing ops), network-ops (DNS changes and route toggles), and platform-release (feature-flag flips). Include the minimum IAM policies to execute the emergency rollback commands in appendix A.
- Logging: capture raw TLS handshake logs from the probes for the 10-minute window around any anomaly — helpful for forensics and to avoid finger-pointing during customer escalations.
- Health probes should use both SNI and direct IP probe modes. Direct IP probe validates the underlying endpoint cert if the CA or DNS has issues.

Marissa/Atlas: if you can give us a short non-prod playground I can run the probes against split-horizon mappings. Prefer a 48h test window.

Laura
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
From: ops@atlas-cloud.com <ops@atlas-cloud.com>

Date: 2026-11-09T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Certificate safeguard & DNS health-probe playbook

Hi all,

Atlas can provision a temporary split-horizon zone and a canary routing group for up to 72 hours in our staging VPCs. The zone will support the SNI-based routing policy Karthik mentioned. A few notes: 

- We'll need the CSR and the intended validity window to configure OCSP/ACME interactions; if you want Atlas to do the rotation we recommend we hold the private key in a customer-managed HSM session (we can do a short-lived token).
- We can expose a probe collector endpoint (HTTPS) in the staging VPC to receive probe telemetry and forward to your Console retention pipeline.

Next steps from our side: send the CSR metadata and preferred test window. We also opened ticket ATLAS-3561 to track the staging setup.

Best,
Atlas Cloud Ops

Date: 2026-11-10T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Certificate safeguard & DNS health-probe playbook

Thanks for looping us in. From Acme Payments' side we care most about: no client-visible interruptions, clear rollback SLAs, and a contact for immediate escalation. A couple of requests: 

- Can you provide a short summary (1-pager) of the rollback SLA (max RTO/RPO) and who to call?
- Will the canary phase route production traffic if our SDK continues to resolve the canonical FQDN? If so, we need to coordinate a scheduled low-traffic window to avoid payment failures.

If you want, we can push a short list of test accounts to whitelist during the staging window to reduce scope.

Jane
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Payments
